title: Project and Pack methods
summary: yoke qa mission host-command --timeout-seconds defaults to 60 and allows at most 900. A --gui-session command that times out has its whole process tree stopped, returns the stdout and stderr it printed before the deadline, and reports gui_command_timeout_stopped as the last stderr line; when it cannot be confirmed gone it reports gui_command_timeout_not_stopped, keeps its output files and names their paths. A Terminal window left open is named gui_command_window_not_closed beside the command's own answer. A Yoke setup, connect or onboard call with a timeout under the 600s browser-approval wait prints the warning host_command_timeout_below_approval_wait. After deployment membership removal, the original execution session can run walk-end on the recorded host under a temporary cleanup lease; teardown deletes staged secrets, restores starting state and records proof while the execution stays aborted. Other sessions, walk-start and host-command remain refused. Guards exempt host-command argv only on a direct call, so a walker never wraps it in its own script. The supported pull step is `-- base64 -i REMOTE_PATH > LOCAL.json`, then decoding the JSON stdout field locally. A refused target in another user's home from a call with no `yoke` invocation names that direct call. A mission host-command can select a companion declared in method_config.machines with --machine NAME; omission targets the retained driver. The server validates all host leases, refuses outside hosts with mission_machine_not_declared, and issues a host_command contract for the companion lease without reset or secret staging. Walk setup, scratch and teardown remain on the driver. Self-host first-boot tokens originate on the companion and stay in its owner-only bundle secrets directory until cleanup.
